content: Over the past several years, the MHSA has undergone significant attention and a series of proposed amendments to address emerging operational risks and tighten accountability structures. An analysis of the legislative trajectory between 2020 and 2024 reveals an overall stable trend in the number of key amendments to the MHSA, with the volume of legislative changes reaching a minimum of 1.0 amendment in 2022 and peaking at a maximum of 4.0 amendments in 2023. In addition to administrative and training reforms, substantial attention was directed toward mitigating long-term occupational health risks, specifically regarding the exposure of mineworkers to hazardous airborne substances. Amendments to Schedule 2 of the MHSA focused heavily on lowering occupational exposure limits, marking a critical intervention in industrial hygiene and preventive occupational medicine. By requiring advanced technological systems to automatically intervene and mitigate the risk of vehicular incidents in dynamic mining environments, the DMRE demonstrated a proactive approach to addressing one of the industry's most persistent fatal risks [32] . Historically, the DMRE has relied on foundational guidelines such as the Code of Practice for change management in mining, published in 2014, which focuses on systematic risk assessments for operational changes to prevent health and safety hazards. While the principles from this 2014 document have likely been integrated into later DMRE directives, its age necessitates an updated approach to reflect present-day standards and technological advancements in risk management [42] . The Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management, which was widely adopted by numerous South African mining operations between 2021 and 2022, introduced rigorous new requirements for the monitoring and risk assessment of tailings facilities [35] . By providing standardized frameworks for risk assessment, hazard identification, and incident reporting, these publications ensure that mining safety services are equipped with the necessary knowledge to implement monitoring mechanisms effectively.
